newsitem.title: EGYPT: Turkish premier off on controversial trip to Libya.
newsitem.headline: Turkish premier off on controversial trip to Libya.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan left Cairo on a controversial trip to Libya on Friday after a two-day visit during which Egypt and Turkey signed agreements on trade and investment.

Erbakan was flying from Cairo to Tunisia and will travel by road across the border to Tripoli, a Turkish official said, ignoring U.S. objections. He cannot fly straight to Libya because of U.N. sanctions.

In a ceremony earlier on Friday, Erbakan and Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri signed the protocol of their joint economic commission and three other agreements -- on trade, on promoting and protecting Turkish and Egyptian investments and on judicial cooperation.

Erbakan told the ceremony Egypt and Turkey would try to increase trade next year to $2 billion, $1 billion in each direction. Current trade is about $380 million a year, 65-35 in favour of Turkish exports to Egypt.
A joint communique released at the ceremony called on Israel to close down the archaeological tunnel it reopened last month near Moslem holy sites in Jersualem.
More than 70 people were killed in protests against the tunnel but Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said it will stay open forever.

"The two prime ministers...expressed their concerns about the events in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza resulting from the opening of the tunnel under al-Aqsa mosque by Israeli authorities. They called on the Israeli government to close the tunnel immediately and not to resort to force," it said.

"The two sides called on the Israeli government to take full responsibilities for agreements reached between Israel and Palestine, to renew without delay and with good intention peace talks in line with the Madrid recommendations and to refrain from any action which threatens the peace talks, including changes in the status of Jerusalem and settlements," it added.
The two men also called for protecting Iraq's territorial integrity and for implementing the U.N. oil-for-food deal to aid the Iraqi people, under economic sanctions for the past six years.

"They stressed the importance they attach to Iraq's territorial integrity, sovereignty and unity. They express their determination that implementation of U.N. resolution 986 (on oil for food)...be accelerated," it said.
Officials travelling with Erbakan have brushed aside criticism of Erbakan's trip to Libya by Washington and his secular coalition partners. Washington terms Libya a sponsor of state terrorism.

"Turkey is an independent country that has the powers and prerogatives to make a decision. We have diplomatic relations with Libya and it is natural that we have commerial ties with Libya," said government spokesman Abdullah Gul.
Turkish officials have already arrived in Tripoli to seek payment of up to $365 million owed to Turkish contractors.
